claims.claim_vi: PostgreSQL lists four phenomena (dirty read, nonrepeatable read, phantom read, serialization anomaly); its Read Uncommitted behaves like Read Committed, its Repeatable Read does not allow phantom reads, which the SQL standard permits because it only says which anomalies must not occur.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Read Committed is the default; each SELECT sees data committed before the query began, so two successive SELECTs in one transaction can see different data.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Applications using Repeatable Read or Serializable must be prepared to retry transactions; read-only transactions never have serialization conflicts at Repeatable Read; Serializable is implemented with Serializable Snapshot Isolation; MVCC stands for Multiversion Concurrency Control.
claims.section: Introduction; Repeatable Read; Serializable Isolation Level
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Measured on PostgreSQL 16.15: at Read Uncommitted and Read Committed T1 read 100 while T2's update to 200 was uncommitted and 200 after it committed, and a row count went 1 then 2; at Repeatable Read and Serializable T1 kept reading 100 and 1 row. In the on-call write-skew test both transactions committed at Repeatable Read leaving 0 on duty; at Serializable the second failed with 'could not serialize access due to read/write dependencies among transactions' leaving 1.
claims.verified_by: Author's own run on 2026-10-18; not repeated on other systems.

claims.claim_vi: Four isolation levels (Serializable, Repeatable Read, Read Committed, Read Uncommitted); isolation is guaranteed by MVCC, which the source names Multi-Version Consistency Control, and locks; an MVCC example with transaction_id and roll_pointer.

design_notes_vi: Bốn thẻ ghi điều T1 thấy ở từng mức, một ví dụ lệch ghi hai bác sĩ, hai lưu ý khi chọn mức. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source expands MVCC as Multi-Version Consistency Control; the lesson uses PostgreSQL's Multiversion Concurrency Control.

The source's MVCC example (hidden transaction_id and roll_pointer columns) is not reproduced; the lesson shows observed behaviour on PostgreSQL instead, including write skew, which the source does not mention.
The source says Serializable runs transactions in sequence; the lesson shows PostgreSQL running them concurrently and aborting one on a detected anomaly.
